item.description:
Security. An unsubscribe link can no longer be aimed at your own network. Nevermore already refused private and local addresses, but it checked the address and then let the system look the name up a second time to open the connection — so a sender running their own DNS could answer with a public address for the check and your router for the connection. The address that passes the check is now the address the connection goes to, on every redirect hop. Certificate checking is untouched.

  • An AI assistant can help you triage. Off by default. It reads your senders and proposes a set worth dropping, each with a reason, in a new Proposed collection. It cannot unsubscribe in bulk, ever — a set of senders is unsubscribed only after you have reviewed that exact set and confirmed it.
  • What each sender costs you. A Size column totalling what their mail occupies, and a forecast of how much more to expect over the next year.
  • A report on how the last month went — which unsubscribes were honoured and which were ignored, without claiming more than the app can observe.
  • Smart selections for the obvious cases: never opened, nothing in a year, one-click capable.
  • Guided app-password setup for your provider, and a Help menu that points at real help.
  • Undo of a trash now puts archived mail back in the archive rather than the inbox, and the unsubscribe results sheet leads with the senders that still need you.

Your header cache migrates automatically, forward-only, with a backup taken first. Nothing asks you to re-authenticate.

The version number catching up to what the app is: no known data-loss bugs, and a verified sandboxed build. The app is unchanged from 0.1.1.

  • Nevermore is now on the Mac App Store, listed as "Nevermore Mail Cleanup". This direct-download build is the same app and keeps updating itself.
  • Support now has its own page, with an email address, so getting help never requires a GitHub account.

Packaging and documentation. The app itself is unchanged from 0.1.0.

  • The app inside the disk image now carries its own stapled notarization ticket, so an update installs cleanly on a Mac that is offline or behind a filter.
  • The privacy policy is published at brooksc.github.io/Nevermore/privacy.html, and now describes this update check.
